shifts.summary: The shift was overall moderate. Reasoning was reported as moderate with candidates feeling confident on statement‑based items. Quantitative section was the toughest, many reported time pressure and difficulty ranging up to hard. English was consistently easy, while GA varied between easy‑moderate and moderate‑difficult.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported no trouble in reasoning, level was fine, and statements were moderate. One report called reasoning easy, another easy to moderate.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA covered current affairs from 2024‑2025 and scheme‑related topics. Some reports found it easy‑moderate, others moderate‑difficult.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant was described as difficult, hard and highly calculative. Time pressure was noted with 25 questions in 15 minutes.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was described as very simple and easy across reports.

intro: On 24 October 2026 the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, with reasoning moderate, quantitative the toughest, English easy and General Awareness ranging from easy‑moderate to moderate‑difficult. Shift 2 received a partial review and was described as moderate to difficult, with quantitative difficult and English moderate; the partial status indicates that the review is limited and needs further corroboration. No usable analysis has been published yet for shift 3, and more candidate evidence is required before a summary can be provided. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, while shift 2 was described as moderate to difficult. Shift 3 has no usable analysis yet, so its difficulty level is not available.

faqs.q: How did candidates perform in the Quantitative section across the shifts on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: In shift 1 candidates found the Quantitative section to be the toughest, reporting time pressure and difficulty up to hard. In shift 2 the Quantitative section was reported as difficult. No data is available for shift 3 at this time.

faqs.q: What does the "partial" status mean for the analysis of shift 2 on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: The "partial" status indicates that a limited review of shift 2 has been published, but the findings need further corroboration before they are considered conclusive.

faqs.q: Is there any usable analysis available for shift 3 of the 24 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published for shift 3 yet. Additional candidate evidence is required before a summary can be released.

faqs.q: Are the reported good attempt figures for the 24 October 2026 shifts official?
faqs.a: The good attempt ranges (70–85 for shift 1 and 62–71 for shift 2) are unofficial figures. SSC normalises scores across shifts, and these numbers should be treated as indicative rather than official.
